title: Understanding language model scaling for protein fitness prediction
methods: structure and biophysical context analysis (ColabFold, MDTraj, Foldseek)

core_conclusion: Bigger protein models are not uniformly better for fitness prediction. Model size, training corpus and stochastic training elements bias the predicted sequence likelihood p(sequence) away from real fitness. Performance is highest when the model-predicted wild-type sequence likelihood sits in a moderate range, where p(sequence) matches evolutionary patterns in homologs; at extreme wild-type likelihoods the model assigns nearly all mutations uniformly low or high likelihood and the fitness landscape collapses. Because larger models systematically predict higher p(sequence), scaling can push a protein out of the useful regime, explaining the observed performance decline beyond a certain model size and making wild-type likelihood a label-free, per-protein model-selection signal.
why_it_matters: Supplies a mechanism for the empirically known protein language model 'scaling wall'; converts the diagnosis into a zero-label per-protein model-selection criterion (wild-type sequence likelihood); reframes high likelihood as corpus saturation rather than biological understanding; carries direct consequences for clinical missense variant interpretation and protein design ranking; and provides a concrete counterexample to scaling-law orthodoxy in a domain where the pretraining objective is only a proxy for the downstream target.
why_nature: Explains why a widely used computational score behaves as it does rather than proposing another architecture - the mechanism-first Analysis format Nature Computational Science favours; sits at the journal's computational-biology / machine-learning / method-evaluation intersection; delivers actionable community guidelines; is anchored to the public ProteinGym benchmark with data, code and per-figure source data deposited on Zenodo; and challenges the 'scale is all you need' narrative with falsifiable evidence as protein foundation models reach 100B parameters.
added_value_to_my_research: Wild-type likelihood as a label-free router -> per-city selection of geospatial foundation models without local ground truth
Landscape-resolution entropy -> diagnostic for over-smoothed accessibility, telehealth and MGWR prediction surfaces
Proxy-objective recalibration -> quantile-mapping and small-label fine-tuning before using pretrained encoders for service-desert ranking
Pretraining-corpus representation audit -> quantifying the geographic digital divide baked into GeoAI foundation models
Retrieval-conditioned local support -> MGWR kernel logic reimplemented as learned cross-city retrieval for physics-informed graph learning
